sections.title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Bessis–Moussa–Villani conjecture for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra equipped with a faithful normal tracial state, constructing a positive Laplace-representation measure.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract and Theorem A claim nonnegative traces of symmetrized words for positive operators and a unique positive measure representing the trace exponential.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state; the BMV positivity statement is for positive operator pairs.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is scoped to finite algebras with the specified trace; it does not assert the corresponding result for arbitrary operator algebras.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors extend a conjecture known for matrix algebras to a finite von Neumann algebra setting and provide a positive-measure representation; three mathematical categories are listed. sections.title: Cutoff on abelian groups
sections.abstract: The authors prove equivalence between cutoff and the product condition for abelian random walks under a logarithmic sparsity restriction, with a sharp mixing-window estimate and examples showing the restriction is optimal.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 gives a quantitative bound on the mixing-window width; the authors derive the cutoff/product-condition equivalence in the stated regime and construct abelian Cayley graphs showing sharpness of the sparsity restriction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sequences of continuous-time random walks on finite abelian groups; inverse transition probabilities grow at most logarithmically with group size. Reversibility is not required.
sections.unique_caveat: The equivalence requires the stated sparsity condition; the paper gives counterexamples near the boundary, so it is not a criterion for every abelian walk.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The preprint reports a long-predicted equivalence, a quantitative mixing-window bound, and examples establishing the sparsity threshold’s optimality. Semantic Scholar current totals: 1 citation and 0 influential citations; no journal reference is listed.

sections.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
sections.abstract: For full-dimensional three-dimensional lattice polytopes with at least three interior lattice points, the authors prove the normalized-volume bound and characterize equality, completing the conjecture in dimension three together with known cases.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.2 states that a full-dimensional lattice polytope in R³ with k ≥ 3 interior lattice points has normalized volume at most 6(k+1), with equality exactly for affine-unimodular copies of the specified Sylvester simplex.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional full-dimensional lattice polytopes; k counts interior lattice points. The equality classification is up to affine unimodular equivalence.
sections.unique_caveat: This paper resolves only dimension three; the conjecture in higher dimensions remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim a complete three-dimensional resolution with an explicit extremal volume and equality classification. Semantic Scholar current totals: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; no journal reference is listed.

sections.title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
sections.abstract: The authors disprove a strong-type one-supremum conjecture with explicit weights and establish logarithmically corrected bounds whose common logarithmic exponent is claimed to be optimal.
sections.claimed_result: For every 1 < p < ∞ the proposed bound fails, with a lower bound of order m(1+log m)^γp, and the paper claims a logarithmically corrected upper bound with optimal common exponent γp = max{1/p,1/p'}.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The strong-type formulation of the one-supremum conjecture; explicit weights, a fixed Hilbert transform, and fixed Riesz transforms in dimensions n ≥ 2.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample addresses the stated one-supremum formulation and weighted operator setting; it does not rule out bounds under different hypotheses or formulations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives both a counterexample for a fixed Hilbert transform and matching sharp logarithmic growth, with a stated extension to Riesz transforms; it is cross-listed in classical analysis and functional analysis. sections.title: Sidorenko Inequalities in Oriented Graphs
sections.abstract: The authors define relative Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs over arbitrary host graphs, characterize connected relatively Sidorenko graphs via weakly norming graphs, and give examples of both types.
sections.claimed_result: The authors characterize connected relatively Sidorenko graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs and exhibit families satisfying the relative Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko inequalities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For an orientation of H, the comparison is between oriented homomorphism counts and 2^{-e(H)} times the homomorphism count of its underlying graph, over every oriented host graph with that underlying graph.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract claims a complete characterization only for the connected relatively Sidorenko class; the anti-Sidorenko side is presented through examples and families, not a full classification.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The preprint broadens the host-graph setting and claims a complete characterization for connected relatively Sidorenko graphs, alongside constructed families. Semantic Scholar current totals: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: New bounds on simplex-avoiding sets in two dimensions
sections.abstract: The authors bound the measure of orthonormal-basis-avoiding subsets of S² by 7/11 and the upper Banach density of unit-equilateral-triangle-avoiding subsets of R² by 9/16, using a geometric fractional chromatic number method.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract gives normalized spherical measure at most 7/11 for sets containing no orthonormal basis and upper Banach density at most 9/16 for sets containing no unit equilateral triangle.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Measurable subsets of S² or R² avoiding the stated three-point configurations; the two density notions differ between the compact and Euclidean settings.
sections.unique_caveat: These are upper bounds, not asserted exact extremal densities; the authors describe the first as the first improvement over the trivial averaging bound and the second as improving the previous best bound.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two explicit improved extremal bounds, a method formulated across compact homogeneous and Euclidean settings, and linked exact rational certificates and verification code. Semantic Scholar current totals: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
sections.abstract: For open subsets of Rᵈ and a specified fractional Sobolev range, the authors prove a capacitary-distance Hardy inequality and show sharpness of its α-exponent and smoothness range.
sections.claimed_result: The paper proves the bound integral over Ω of |u(x)|^p divided by d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}, at most C α^{-p'} times the fractional Sobolev seminorm [u]_{s,p}^p, for u in C_c^∞(Ω); C depends only on d,s,p. It also claims sharpness of the α exponent and smoothness range.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Ω is open in Rᵈ, α ∈ (0,1], and u is smooth with compact support in Ω; dα,s,p is defined from a relative fractional capacity threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: The inequality is stated for compactly supported smooth functions and the given fractional parameter range; it does not by itself state boundary regularity or extension results for broader function classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result states explicit sharp parameter dependence and is cross-listed across PDE, classical analysis, and functional analysis. Semantic Scholar current totals: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
sections.abstract: Using local flag algebras, the author proves that every graph with sufficiently large maximum degree Δ has strong chromatic index at most 1.642Δ², improving the prior stated bound of 1.73Δ².
sections.claimed_result: For every graph G of sufficiently large maximum degree Δ, χ′s(G) ≤ 1.642Δ².
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs with sufficiently large maximum degree; a strong edge coloring separates edges that are incident or joined by a third edge.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is asymptotic in the maximum degree and gives an upper bound, not an exact value for the strong chromatic index.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a numerical improvement over an explicit previous bound and names the local flag algebra technique. Semantic Scholar current totals: 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
sections.abstract: The authors propose an inexact SVRG method for constrained convex finite-sum problems that improves the claimed first-order oracle complexity for solutions with deterministically bounded constraint violation and an expected optimality gap.
sections.claimed_result: The proposed inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method improves the previously best-known first-order oracle complexity for ε-surely feasible stochastic optimal solutions; in a single-objective case it reduces to a deterministic first-order method for convex conic optimization.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Constrained convex finite-sum optimization; feasibility violation is deterministically bounded by ε and expected optimality gap by ε. Numerical results are described as preliminary.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not give the numerical complexity expressions, and its performance advantage in the deterministic case is conditional on constraint-gradient and projection costs being cheaper than objective-gradient evaluation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract claims an improved oracle complexity for a precisely constrained solution concept; the arXiv listing says accepted by SIAM Journal on Optimization, and the paper cross-lists machine learning.
